name: Kitgenix Order Tracking for WooCommerce
author: Kitgenix

sections.description:
Kitgenix Order Tracking for WooCommerce lets you attach one or more tracking numbers to WooCommerce orders, include tracking details in emails, and offer customers a branded tracking page with an optional delivery route map.

The plugin focuses on clarity for customers and speed for store owners:

  • Add multiple tracking numbers per order (partial shipments, split parcels, multiple carriers)
  • Show carrier name, tracking number, and a direct tracking link
  • Display a public tracking form on any page via shortcode
  • Optionally display a delivery route map using OpenStreetMap + Leaflet (no API key)

Key Features

  • Multiple tracking numbers per order

    • Add as many tracking entries as you need
    • Each entry stores carrier, tracking number and tracking URL

  • Built-in carrier presets

    • DPD UK
    • DPD Ireland
    • DHL
    • Royal Mail
    • An Post
    • Parcelforce
    • Woodside Distribution
    • Other carrier option for custom URLs

  • Automatic tracking links

    • Uses predefined URL patterns per carrier
    • Generates direct “Track shipment” links for customers

  • Branded public tracking page

    • Shortcode: [kitgenix_tracking_form]
    • Customers enter order number + email (or similar identifiers) to view tracking
    • Shows carrier logos, tracking numbers and links

  • WooCommerce email integration

    • Adds tracking block to Completed Order email
    • Includes tracking details in the custom Kitgenix Partially Shipped email
    • Designed to be readable on desktop and mobile

  • Optional delivery route map

    • Uses OpenStreetMap + Leaflet (bundled)
    • No Google Maps or API key required
    • Shows route from store location to customer shipping address (approximate)

  • WooCommerce native UI

    • Order edit screen panel: Kitgenix Order Tracking
    • Add/edit/remove tracking entries inline
    • Works with standard WooCommerce order statuses and flows

  • Performance and compatibility

    • Frontend assets loaded only on tracking pages and emails
    • Compatible with WooCommerce 10+, WordPress 6.8+ and PHP 7.0–8.x

Ideal for stores that ship orders in multiple parcels, use different carriers per order, or want to give customers a clean, branded way to check tracking.

How It Works

  1. Add tracking to orders
    On the WooCommerce Edit Order screen, use the Kitgenix Order Tracking panel to add one or more tracking numbers. Choose a carrier from the list or select Other and enter a custom link.

  2. Send tracking emails
    When you mark an order as Completed or send a Partially Shipped email, the plugin attaches a tracking section with carrier name, tracking number and a direct link.

  3. Customer self-service tracking
    Place the [kitgenix_tracking_form] shortcode on a page. Customers can enter their details, see tracking numbers, carriers and links, and (optionally) view a route map.

  4. Optional route map
    When enabled, the tracking page displays an interactive map powered by OpenStreetMap + Leaflet, drawing an approximate route between your store and the customer address.

Quick Start

  1. Install and activate Kitgenix Order Tracking for WooCommerce.
  2. Go to WooCommerce → Orders, open any order.
  3. Find the Kitgenix Order Tracking panel on the order edit screen.
  4. Click Add tracking and select a carrier, enter the tracking number (and custom URL if needed).
  5. Save the order.
  6. Create a new WordPress page (e.g. “Track Your Order”) and add the shortcode:
    [kitgenix_tracking_form].
  7. Share this page with customers (menu link, footer link, email link, etc.).

Features in Detail

Multiple Tracking Numbers

  • Add more than one tracking number to the same order (e.g. split shipments, multiple boxes, replacements).
  • Each tracking line includes:
    • Carrier
    • Tracking number
    • Tracking URL (auto-generated or custom)
  • Remove or update entries at any time from the order editor.

Carrier Presets and Logos

  • Predefined carriers with URL patterns and icons for:
    • DPD UK
    • DPD Ireland
    • DHL
    • Royal Mail
    • An Post
    • Parcelforce
    • Woodside Distribution
  • Other carrier option for any custom service; paste your own tracking URL.
  • Carrier icons are displayed on the tracking page and in supported emails.

Public Tracking Form

  • Shortcode: [kitgenix_tracking_form]
  • Place on any page or in a block/shortcode widget.
  • Customers typically enter:
    • Their order number
    • Their billing email address
  • The plugin then:
    • Locates the matching order
    • Displays associated tracking entries (carrier, number, link)
    • Optionally shows the route map.

Email Integration

  • Completed Order email
    If tracking entries exist, a tracking section is appended with all tracking numbers and links.

  • Kitgenix Partially Shipped email
    Custom WooCommerce email type provided by the plugin. Useful when:

    • Only part of the order has shipped
    • You want to send tracking early, before completion

  • The email layout is designed to be clear and minimal, working well in most email clients.

Route Map (OpenStreetMap + Leaflet)

  • Optional, can be enabled via plugin settings (if provided) or hooked in by developers.
  • Uses the bundled Leaflet library and OpenStreetMap tiles.
  • Shows an approximate route between your store location and the customer shipping address.
  • No external API keys or paid services required.

Minimum Requirements

  • WordPress 5.0 or higher
  • WooCommerce (recent stable version, 10+ recommended)
  • PHP 7.0 or higher

Developers

  • Text domain: kitgenix-order-tracking-for-woocommerce (POT file included in languages/).
  • Core plugin bootstrap: kitgenix-order-tracking-for-woocommerce.php.
  • Main plugin class and setup: includes/Plugin.php.
  • Admin order UI and meta box handling: includes/Admin/Order_Meta_Box.php.
  • Order tracking logic and lookup: includes/Orders/Order_Tracking.php.
  • Carrier definitions and helpers: includes/Support/Carriers.php.
  • Frontend shortcode and tracking page: includes/Frontend/Shortcodes.php.
  • Email integration and custom email class: includes/Emails/ (including Partially Shipped email template files in templates/emails/).
  • Frontend assets (CSS/JS, Leaflet map): assets/.

Developers can extend or customise behaviour via standard WooCommerce hooks and filters, or by overriding email templates in a theme.

Translations

This plugin is translation-ready. A POT file is included in languages/ so translators can generate MO/PO files for their locale.

  • Text domain: kitgenix-order-tracking-for-woocommerce
  • POT file location: languages/kitgenix-order-tracking-for-woocommerce.pot

You can use tools like Poedit or Loco Translate, or contribute via the WordPress.org translation platform.

Data Handling

  • Tracking details are stored as order meta attached to WooCommerce orders.
  • No custom database tables are created.
  • Uninstalling the plugin does not automatically remove existing tracking meta; remove order meta if you need to purge it.
  • The plugin itself does not set cookies or perform user tracking. Carrier links lead to external sites; review each carrier’s privacy policy.

External Services

This plugin may connect to external carrier tracking websites when customers click tracking links or when route maps request map tiles. It uses:

  • Carrier tracking URLs (varies per carrier, e.g. DPD, DHL, Royal Mail, An Post, Parcelforce, Woodside Distribution)
  • OpenStreetMap tiles and Leaflet JavaScript/CSS for map display

No personal data is sent by the plugin itself beyond what is required in the tracking URL and map requests. Review each carrier’s and OpenStreetMap/Leaflet’s terms and privacy policies for details.

Trademark Notice

All carrier names and logos (DPD, DHL, Royal Mail, An Post, Parcelforce, Woodside Distribution and others) are trademarks of their respective owners. This plugin is not affiliated with or endorsed by any carrier.

Copyright

Kitgenix Order Tracking for WooCommerce is built by Kitgenix.

Credits

  • Built with WooCommerce and WordPress.
  • Map rendering powered by Leaflet and OpenStreetMap.
  • Built by https://kitgenix.com.

Support Development

If this plugin helps you keep customers informed and reduce support tickets, you can support ongoing development here:

https://buymeacoffee.com/kitgenix
sections.installation:
1. Install via Plugins → Add New and search for “Kitgenix Order Tracking for WooCommerce”, or upload the plugin folder kitgenix-order-tracking-for-woocommerce to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin from the Plugins screen.
  3. Open WooCommerce → Orders and edit any order.
  4. Use the Kitgenix Order Tracking panel to add tracking numbers and carriers.
  5. Create a tracking page using the shortcode:
    [kitgenix_tracking_form].
  6. Optionally test by placing a test order and completing it to see tracking details in the Completed Order email.
sections.faq:
Does the plugin support multiple tracking numbers per order?

Yes. You can add as many tracking numbers as required for a single order. Each tracking number can use the same or a different carrier.

Which carriers are supported?

The plugin includes built-in support for major UK and Ireland carriers:

  • DPD UK
  • DPD Ireland
  • DHL
  • Royal Mail
  • An Post
  • Parcelforce
  • Woodside Distribution

You can also choose Other and paste a custom tracking URL for any carrier or courier service.

Do customers receive tracking emails automatically?

Yes. When tracking entries exist for an order, tracking details are automatically included in:

  • WooCommerce Completed Order email
  • The custom Kitgenix Partially Shipped email provided by the plugin

Tracking details are not showing in the Completed Order email. What can I check?

If tracking isn’t appearing:

  • Confirm the order has at least one tracking entry saved.
  • Ensure the order status is set to Completed and the email is enabled under WooCommerce → Settings → Emails.
  • Check if your theme or another plugin overrides the Completed Order email template or removes the relevant hooks.
  • If you use a custom email workflow, send the Kitgenix Partially Shipped email to verify tracking output.

Can customers check their tracking online without logging in?

Yes. Place the shortcode [kitgenix_tracking_form] on any public page (e.g. Track Your Order). Customers can enter their order details and view tracking numbers and links.

The `[kitgenix_tracking_form]` shortcode is not rendering.

Make sure the plugin is active and the shortcode is added to the page content (block or classic editor). If you use a page builder, insert a shortcode/block element and paste [kitgenix_tracking_form]. Clear caches (site/CDN) if the page is cached.

Do I need a Google Maps API key for the route map?

No. The plugin uses OpenStreetMap + Leaflet, which are free and do not require an API key.

The route map does not load or is blank.

Check your browser console for errors and ensure frontend assets are loading on the tracking page. The map uses bundled Leaflet and OpenStreetMap tiles—no API key is required. If you use aggressive caching or a Content Security Policy, allow the Leaflet assets and OSM tiles.

Is this compatible with my theme and page builder?

The tracking form and results are rendered using standard WooCommerce and WordPress markup, so they work with most themes and page builders. You can further style the tracking page with custom CSS if needed.

Can I style the tracking section?

Yes. Use your theme’s custom CSS or a customizer to style the tracking form and results. Elements are structured with simple classes, so it’s straightforward to apply brand styles.

Does this plugin create or manage shipments in WooCommerce?

No. The plugin does not create separate shipment records or alter WooCommerce’s core order status logic. It simply attaches tracking data to existing orders and displays it to customers.

A carrier link looks incorrect or my carrier is not listed.

Use the Other carrier option and paste a custom tracking URL. You can also extend carriers via WooCommerce hooks/filters if you’re a developer.

Is the plugin GDPR friendly?

The plugin itself does not add cookies or perform tracking. It uses data already stored in the WooCommerce order (such as order number and email) to look up tracking information. Carrier links may lead to external sites; review each carrier’s privacy policy for your legal requirements.
